chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas from Abu Shu'ayb from Abu Jamilah from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is the meaning of the man's saying:
All the pure prayers and good words are for Allah

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.التَّحِيَّاتُ: The pure prayers and good words (a specific phrase in the Tashahhud)
key_terms.الْمُلْكُ: The dominion / The kingdom / The authority

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'Al-tahiyyatu lillah' mean in the context of Islamic prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates that 'Al-tahiyyatu lillah' signifies 'Al-mulku lillah' (Dominion belongs to Allah), linking the concept of divine worship (tahiyyah) directly to God's absolute sovereignty. This interpretation underscores the Shia understanding of the Tashahhud as an affirmation of Allah's exclusive rule, a theme deeply rooted in the Quranic verses regarding His dominion over all creation.
